cohort: 101 primiparous pregnant women (48 with delayed cord clamping, 53 with early cord clamping) without high-risk pregnancies, giving vaginal birth at 38-42 weeks gestation.
finding: Delayed umbilical cord clamping positively affected newborn oxygen saturation values (higher at 1, 5, and 10 minutes) and LATCH breastfeeding scores compared to early cord clamping.
